To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) transitive node similarity is an effective measure of similarity for signed social networks, (ii) it is more accurate than existing measures, (iii) the transitive node similarity method is time efficient, (iv) the transitive similarity method is applicable to both directed and undirected networks, (v) it can be used for signed networks, and (vi) it is applicable to real social networks, such as Facebook and Hi5.
transitive node similarity can effectively predict missing positive and negative links and it can be used for friend recommendation.
transitive node similarity is a promising technique for predicting and recommending links, and that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of both accuracy and efficiency.
